steps.name: QC, sensitivity check, DESeq2 differential expression
caveats: Salmon counts may be uncorrected for transcript length; for a two-group between-sample design this affects only which genes are filterable, not the DE test — state this explicitly
12,000 genes suggests a filtered/quantified feature set; verify no duplicate or NA symbols before testing
n=6 per arm: interpret padj cautiously; report nominal p-values alongside
steps.context: Files: counts.csv (12,000 x 13) and metadata.csv (12 x 2). Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Caveat: sample_01 library size ~4x below median.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (AD lesional) and control skin, and does the low-depth sample_01 drive any of the calls?
steps.description: Load counts.csv and metadata.csv, verify sample/condition alignment, prefilter low-count genes, build a DESeq2 dataset with design ~condition, run size-factor estimation and the treated-vs-control Wald test with independent filtering. Explicitly profile sample_01: library size, size factor, Cook's distances, PCA position. Then rerun DE dropping sample_01 and report per-gene log2FC/padj concordance so conclusions are shown to be robust (or not) to the shallow sample. Do not silently exclude it.
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 runs on the 12x12,000 count matrix with design ~condition
size factors reported; sample_01 flagged with its factor and post-normalization profile
Full-cohort and leave-one-out (drop sample_01) DE tables both produced; per-gene agreement summarized
Results table with gene symbol, log2FC, lfcSE, stat, p-value, padj exported as CSV
Volcano plot and sample-distance/PCA plot written

steps.name: Hallmark pathway enrichment (GSEA + ORA)
caveats: With n=6 per arm the ranking is noisy; report leading-edge sizes and avoid over-interpreting borderline NES
Gene universe for ORA must be the filtered tested genes, not all 12,000 rows
Check that count row identifiers are HGNC symbols; if Ensembl/Entrez, map via the staged human UniProt id-mapping table before scoring
steps.context: Reference: /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols). Input: DE stat table from T1S1 (both full and sample_01-dropped versions — pathway calls should be checked against both to confirm the shallow sample does not flip pathway directions).
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways shift between treated and control skin, and in which direction?
steps.description: Run (a) fgsea preranked GSEA on the full DE ranking (Wald statistic) against the 50 human hallmark sets and (b) over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler/fgsea) of the FDR<0.05 DE gene list. Report NES, FDR, and leading-edge genes per hallmark set, restricted to sets with adequate overlap. Compare full-cohort vs sample_01-dropped rankings for direction consistency of significant sets.
acceptance_criteria: Preranked GSEA against the staged human Hallmark GMT completed with permutation-style null; NES and FDR reported per set
ORA on FDR<0.05 DE genes against the same GMT with hypergeometric FDR; gene-set sizes and overlaps reported
Direction (UP/DN per set) and top leading-edge genes reported for significant hallmarks
Overlap between GSEA and ORA hits explicitly listed; discordances flagged
If the hallmark GMT is unavailable at run time, the step reports the gap and reruns against the staged WikiPathways human GMT rather than failing

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human skin bulk RNA-seq samples (6 AD lesional/treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), gene-level Salmon counts for 12,000 genes. DESeq2 is the appropriate DE engine for raw counts at n=6 per arm; it handles the shallow library (sample_01, ~4x below median) via size-factor normalization, but that sample's influence must be explicitly quantified with leave-one-out DE rather than silently dropped or silently kept. DE results (ranked by Wald statistic, plus an FDR significant set) feed two complementary pathway read-outs against the staged MSigDB 2026.1 human Hallmark GMT: preranked GSEA (robust to the small significant-gene count) and ORA on FDR<0.05 genes, with consistency between the two reported. Identities are HGNC symbols; counts.csv row keys are checked and mapped if needed via the staged human UniProt/annotation resources.
